hints: Notice that nitric acid does two different jobs here, some of it oxidises copper while the rest just provides nitrate ions for the blue solution.
Start with the redox change: each Cu loses 2 electrons to form $\text{Cu}^{2+}$, while each N in $\text{HNO}_3$ gains 3 electrons to go from +5 to +2 in NO.
Balance the electrons lost and gained to link Cu and NO in a 3 to 2 ratio, then add the extra spectator $\text{HNO}_3$ needed to make $\text{Cu(NO}_3)_2$ and balance H with water.
walkthrough:
**Spot the oxidation and reduction**

Think like a teacher with your student. Copper metal becomes blue $\text{Cu}^{2+}$, so it is oxidised. Nitrogen in nitric acid becomes NO, so it is reduced.

Oxidation: $\text{Cu} \rightarrow \text{Cu}^{2+} + 2e^{-}$
Reduction: $\text{N}(+5) + 3e^{-} \rightarrow \text{N}(+2)$

**Balance the electrons to get p and t**

To make electrons lost equal electrons gained, we need a common multiple of 2 and 3, which is 6. So we need 3 Cu atoms and 2 N atoms reduced.
$$3\text{Cu} \rightarrow 3\text{Cu}^{2+} + 6e^{-}$$
$$2\text{HNO}_3 + 6e^{-} \rightarrow 2\text{NO}$$
This tells us $p = 3$ and $t = 2$.

**Add the spectator acid and finish balancing**

The $3\text{Cu}^{2+}$ ions need 6 nitrate ions to make $3\text{Cu(NO}_3)_2$, so $r = 3$. That needs 6 more $\text{HNO}_3$ as acid, on top of the 2 used for oxidation.
$$q = 2 + 6 = 8$$
Finally balance H and O with water. 8 H on the left needs 4 $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ on the right, so $s = 4$. Check O: $8 \times 3 = 24$ on left, and $(3 \times 6) + 4 + 2 = 24$ on right. Balanced!
$$3\text{Cu} + 8\text{HNO}_3 \rightarrow 3\text{Cu(NO}_3)_2 + 4\text{H}_2\text{O} + 2\text{NO}$$

options.A: Unbalanced for O and electrons. Left has 12 O but right has only 10 O. One Cu cannot supply enough electrons to make two NO molecules, which need 6 electrons but Cu gives only 2.
options.B: Close but fails the atom check. H and N balance, but O does not: 18 on left versus 17 on right. The electron balance is also wrong, 2 Cu give 4 electrons but 2 NO need 6 electrons.
options.C: H and N balance but O fails badly: 24 on left versus 20 on right. It doubles the NO without doubling the Cu correctly, so electrons do not balance (4 electrons lost versus 12 gained).
options.D: Fully balanced for all atoms and charge. Cu: 3 = 3, H: 8 = 8, N: 8 = 6 + 2, O: 24 = 24. Electrons also balance with 6 lost by 3 Cu and 6 gained to make 2 NO.
